reason: The text contains only two named characters: YHWH (God) and Moses (Mōsheh). YHWH is the supreme authority giving commandments to the people. Moses is the designated leader of the Israelites who receives God's instructions to convey to the community. All other figures mentioned are referred to generically (hā'ām = 'the people,' 'īsh = 'a man') without individual names. Both named characters hold positions of authority and leadership.
